key_concepts: Food enters the body through the mouth and is chewed by teeth.
Saliva in the mouth begins chemical breakdown of carbohydrates.
The pharynx and esophagus move food toward the stomach.
The stomach churns food with gastric juices to form chyme and begins protein breakdown.
The small intestine mixes chyme with digestive juices and absorbs nutrients, vitamins, min
The liver produces bile that emulsifies fats, the gallbladder stores and releases bile, an
The large intestine absorbs water and electrolytes and propels feces toward the rectum.
The rectum stores stool until it is eliminated through the anus.
Food travels in order from the mouth to the pharynx, esophagus, stomach, small intestine,
Digestion changes food into forms the body can use.
